messages:
olivia: deploybot flagged a p95 latency regression on inference-api canary (eu-west-1) after rolling v2.10.0-canary. deploybot suggests rollback to v2.9.1 or pin. need ops decision.

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary signal for inference-api@eu-west-1. p95 latency +48% vs baseline over 5m (baseline 1.10s -> 1.63s). error_rate stable (0.08%). canary traffic 5%. auto-rollback rules: p95_delta>30% AND error_rate>0.5% => NOT met. recommending manual review.

sameer: copying. is this across all hosts or a noisy subset? any OOMs or gRPC retries in logs?

maya: looking at logs now — saw KV cache miss storm on two pods, latency spike aligns with a kernel-path switch in runtime k3. no OOMs. stacktrace shows increased memcopy time after kernel selection.

sam: any dedicated/reserved pools hitting this canary? need to avoid impacting reserved customers.

olivia: no dedicated pools affected; this is hosted canary slice only. suggestion: do targeted rollback/traffic reduction + pin previous stable to validate. manual rollback preferable since auto conditions didn't trigger.

ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK (extract):
1) reduce canary traffic to 1%
2) pin canary route to previous release (v2.9.1)
3) monitor p95, p99, and KV cache miss rate for 10m
4) if metrics recover -> rollforward after kernel-flag revert in pipeline
5) if metrics worsen -> full rollback and incident channel

sameer: i can execute the traffic reduction. command I'm going to run: 
```
deployctl update-split --service inference-api --region eu-west-1 --from v2.10.0-canary --to v2.9.1 --traffic 1%
```

deploy-bot: INFO: starting traffic change: 5% -> 1% (eu-west-1). watch p95 for 3 minutes. escalation condition: p95 > 1.3s after 3m -> manual rollback.

maya: after traffic drop, p95 trending down to 1.15s and KV cache miss rate back to baseline. looks promising.

sam: can we pin v2.9.1 for the canary route so the remainder 1% stays stable?

olivia: done — pinned canary to v2.9.1. drafting short comms to support + product. also adding note to release notes: reverted runtime kernel-selection flag change for canary.

maya: PR for rollback fix: https://git.example.com/r/redwood/runtime/merge/789 — removes k3 default kernel swap for now. adding test to prevent swap on low-canary traffic.

sameer: for postmortem: investigate why kernel selection change propagated to canary without extra gating. action: add an explicit rollout-guard for kernel-selection flags and a deploybot metric gate for p95-only thresholds that can trigger auto-rollback.

olivia: agreed. action items assigned: 1) revert kernel flag in rollout pipeline (olivia) 2) add p95-only auto-rollback gate in deploybot (sameer) 3) write postmortem + incident timeline (olivia) 4) QA test for kernel-selection guard (maya). I'll update the changelog and ping support.

sam: tagging support and cs: @support @cs. leaving a short blurb for customers: we reverted a runtime kernel selection change in canary that increased tail latency for a small slice of traffic — no dedicated customers impacted.

olivia: we will keep canary pinned until we validate a safe kernel-selection path. closing this thread once ops-runbook confirm metrics stable for 30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

sameer: noted. will follow up on deploybot gating next week.

sam: nice quick turnaround.

olivia: closing notes: manual rollback executed (partial traffic -> pin). no auto-rollback triggered due to conservative error_rate gate. recommend revisiting gates -> :eyes:
